newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa Catholics deny paying for abortion.
newsitem.headline: South Africa Catholics deny paying for abortion.

text.p: South Africa's Roman Catholic Church, in the centre of an emotional debate on liberalising the country's abortion laws, denied on Thursday that it had paid for a woman to end a pregnancy resulting from sex with a priest.
The woman told a parliamentary debate on abortion on Wednesday that she had a year-long love affair with a priest and that a bishop had paid her hospital bills when she needed an abortion.

"At no point did any member of the Catholic hierarchy who was aware of my special circumstances intervene or offer to help me (in a way) that could prevent me having an abortion," said the woman, who could not be identified.
But church spokesman Sydney Duval rejected the accusation.
"The bishop involved categorically denies that he paid for any abortion...He spoke to her only after she had told him that she had the abortion."
Duval said the bishop, after consulting other priests, had acted out of compassion in agreeing that she should seek psychological help.
"All he paid for was her counselling. The church had nothing to do with her having an abortion," Duval said.

The National Assembly will vote on October 29 on whether to relax the abortion law from one of the world's strictest to among the most liberal. The bill goes to the Senate next month and will be adopted if passed by both houses.

At present only about 1,000 women a year qualify for legal abortions. The bill proposes abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy to help the estimated 50,000 women who enter hospital every year after botched backstreet abortions.
